events.name: Dermot's Taste of Ireland
events.description: Dermot reaches Donegal Town, discovering a place where Irish tradition and global flavours sit side by side. His day begins at family-run Hannah Hats, where he's fitted in iconic Donegal tweed and learns why this rugged corner of Ireland became famous for its flecked fabric. He visits Chandpur, widely regarded as Ireland's best curry house, where he and Bangladeshi-born chef Rana cook railway curry using outstanding local lamb and potatoes. For pudding, Dermot bakes a classic Irish apple pie with chef Brian McDermott, who explain how the rain improves local produce

events.name: Dermot's Taste of Ireland
events.description: Dermot reaches Donegal Town, discovering a place where Irish tradition and global flavours sit side by side. His day begins at family-run Hannah Hats, where he's fitted in iconic Donegal tweed and learns why this rugged corner of Ireland became famous for its flecked fabric. He visits Chandpur, widely regarded as Ireland's best curry house, where he and Bangladeshi-born chef Rana cook railway curry using outstanding local lamb and potatoes. For pudding, Dermot bakes a classic Irish apple pie with chef Brian McDermott, who explain how the rain improves local produce

events.name: Dermot's Taste of Ireland
events.description: Dermot reaches Donegal Town, discovering a place where Irish tradition and global flavours sit side by side. His day begins at family-run Hannah Hats, where he's fitted in iconic Donegal tweed and learns why this rugged corner of Ireland became famous for its flecked fabric. He visits Chandpur, widely regarded as Ireland's best curry house, where he and Bangladeshi-born chef Rana cook railway curry using outstanding local lamb and potatoes. For pudding, Dermot bakes a classic Irish apple pie with chef Brian McDermott, who explain how the rain improves local produce

events.name: Dermot's Taste of Ireland
events.description: Dermot reaches Donegal Town, discovering a place where Irish tradition and global flavours sit side by side. His day begins at family-run Hannah Hats, where he's fitted in iconic Donegal tweed and learns why this rugged corner of Ireland became famous for its flecked fabric. He visits Chandpur, widely regarded as Ireland's best curry house, where he and Bangladeshi-born chef Rana cook railway curry using outstanding local lamb and potatoes. For pudding, Dermot bakes a classic Irish apple pie with chef Brian McDermott, who explain how the rain improves local produce

events.name: Love Your Garden

Alan Titchmarsh's challenge is to create a more child-friendly garden for their terraced home in Tonbridge, and his first task is to make a shady environment so the kids can spend time outside in the day. After that, he and the team come up with a bespoke lighting system for the evenings, acoustic fencing to cut down the noise from a nearby railway line, and an area for the parents

Lee Burkhill and Flo Headlam pool their efforts to create an entertainment space in the middle of the garden with a central patio featuring bespoke screesn and L-shaped benches. Flo mucks in with a planting area to draw attention from the giant walls and herb garden by the back door

events.name: Love Your Garden
events.description: Alan Titchmarsh and the horticultural experts come to the aid of Vicky and Simon Pyne, whose daughter Alice died of cancer in January 2013. Alice's story was reported around the world after she created an online list of things she wanted to do or achieve in her final years, while raising thousands of pounds for charity. The team plans to bring the best of the Cumbrian landscape to the Pynes' awkwardly shaped garden, complete with a refuge for their 14-year-old daughter Milly, who has faced her own health problems over the years

events.name: Love Your Garden
events.description: The green-fingered team returns with more surprise garden makeovers for deserving people across the nation. Darren and Lesley Chan's youngest daughter Amelie was born with Charge syndrome - a debilitating genetic condition that has left her deaf, partially sighted and in need of constant care. Alan Titchmarsh sets out to transform the Manchester family's neglected outdoor space, calling in David Domoney, Frances Tophill and Katie Rushworth to introduce sensory planting for the 10-year-old, a shade-loving border and a multifunction pathway made from areas of decking, artificial turf and paving

events.name: This Farming Life
events.description: As the days grow longer, the MacDonalds round up their pregnant Highland cattle on the tiny island of Vallay, off North Uist, for a pre-natal check up and vitamin boost. In the Cairngorms, Jenni's new alpaca arena is finally finished, which means her menagerie of alpacas, donkeys and goats must be moved to their new home. Nikki and Ollie speculate to accumulate in Moray, splashing out on a new honesty shack.

events.name: Love Your Garden
events.description: Kent couple Lou and Andy Webb have two young children affected by a rare genetic condition that severely restricts their eyesight, meaning they only see in black and white and have to wear special goggles in sunlight. Alan Titchmarsh's challenge is to create a more child-friendly garden for their terraced home in Tonbridge, and his first task is to make a shady environment so the kids can spend time outside in the day. After that, he and the team come up with a bespoke lighting system for the evenings, acoustic fencing to cut down the noise from a nearby railway line, and an area for the parents

events.name: Garden Rescue
events.description: In Uttoxeter, east Staffordshire, Shail and Cecilia long for a garden that reminds them of growing up in the countryside of India. However, the new-build garden they own is a featureless sloping plot. Lee Burkhill and Flo Headlam pool their efforts to create an entertainment space in the middle of the garden with a central patio featuring bespoke screesn and L-shaped benches. Lee adds a home-made tandoor for the family to cook together and a food prep area and vegetable growing beds. Flo mucks in with a planting area to draw attention from the giant walls and herb garden by the back door

The team plans to bring the best of the Cumbrian landscape to the Pynes' awkwardly shaped garden, complete with a refuge for their 14-year-old daughter Milly, who has faced her own health problems over the years

events.name: Garden Rescue
events.description: In Uttoxeter, east Staffordshire, Shail and Cecilia long for a garden that reminds them of growing up in the countryside of India. However, the new-build garden they own is a featureless sloping plot. Lee Burkhill and Flo Headlam pool their efforts to create an entertainment space in the middle of the garden with a central patio featuring bespoke screesn and L-shaped benches. Lee adds a home-made tandoor for the family to cook together and a food prep area and vegetable growing beds. Flo mucks in with a planting area to draw attention from the giant walls and herb garden by the back door

Alan Titchmarsh sets out to transform the Manchester family's neglected outdoor space, calling in David Domoney, Frances Tophill and Katie Rushworth to introduce sensory planting for the 10-year-old, a shade-loving border and a multifunction pathway made from areas of decking, artificial turf and paving
